RUB amount).\n   480→    #[wasm_bindgen]\n   481→    pub fn update_cbr_rates_from_api(&mut self, date: &str, rates_json: &str) -> usize {\n   482→        let rates: std::collections::HashMap<String, 575→\n   576→    /// Generates plot data for an integral expression.\n   577→    fn generate_plot_data_for_integral(&mut self, input: &str) -> Option<PlotData> {\n   578→        // Try to parse and extract the integrand for plotting\n   579→        let expr = self.parser.parse(input).ok()?;\n   580→\n   581→        if let types::Expression::IndefiniteIntegral {\n   582→            integrand,\n   583→            variable,\n   584→        } = expr\n   585→        {\n   586→            // Generate plot points for the integrand\n   587→            let mut x_values = Vec::new();\n   588→ 593→            let x_max = 10.0;\n   594→            let step = (x_max - x_min) / f64::from(num_points);\n   595→\n   596→            for i in 0..=num_points {\n   597→                let x = 705→        self.parser.evaluate(expr)\n   706→    }\n   707→\n   708→    /// Loads a historical exchange rate from .lino format content.\n   709→    ///\n   710→    /// The .lino format for rates:\n             source = Some(src.to_string());\n   746→            }\n   747→        }\n   748→\n   749→        let from = from_currency.ok_or(\"Missing 'from' currency\")?;\n   750→        let to = 136→    /// Adds two values with optional date context for historical currency conversion.\n   137→    pub fn add_at_date(\n   138→        &self,\n   139→        other: &Self,\n   140→ Ok(Value::duration(s1 + s2))\n   170→            }\n   171→            _ => Err(CalculatorError::InvalidOperation(format!(\n   172→                \"Cannot add {} and {}\",\n   173→                self.type_name(),\n   174→                other.type_name()\n   175→            ))),\n   176→        }\n   177→    }\n   178→\n   179→    fn add_rationals(\n   180→        &self,\n   181→        a: Rational,\n   182→        b: Rational,\n   183→        other: &Self,\n   184→        currency_db: &mut CurrencyDatabase,\n   185→        date: Option<&DateTime>,\n   186→    ) -> Result<Self, CalculatorError> {\n   187→        match (&self.unit, &other.unit) {\n   188→            (Unit::None, Unit::None) => Ok(Value::rational(a + b)),\n   189→            (Unit::None, unit) | (unit, Unit::None) => {\n   190→                Ok(Value::rational_with_unit(a + b, unit.clone()))\n   191→            }\n   192→            // Same currency\n   193→            (Unit::Currency(c1), Unit::Currency(c2)) if c1 == c2 => {\n   194→                Ok(Value::rational_with_unit(a + b, self.unit.clone()))\n   195→            }\n   196→            // Different currencies - need conversion (uses Decimal for approximation)\n   197→            (Unit::Currency(c1), Unit::Currency(c2)) => {\n   198→                let a_dec = a.to_decimal();\n   199→                let b_dec = b.to_decimal();\n   200→                // Use historical rate if date is provided\n   201→                let converted = if let Some(dt) = date {\n   202→                    currency_db.convert_at_date(b_dec.to_f64(), c2, c1, dt)?\n   203→                } else {\n   204→                    currency_db.convert(b_dec.to_f64(), c2, c1)?\n   205→                };\n   206→                let converted_decimal = Decimal::from_f64(converted);\n   207→                Ok(Value::currency(a_dec + converted_decimal, c1))\n   208→            }\n   209→            // Mass + different mass unit (convert to first unit's type)\n   210→            (Unit::Mass(m1), Unit::Mass(m2)) if m1 != m2 => {\n   211→                let a_val = a.to_f64();\n   212→                let b_val = b.to_f64();\n   213→                let b_converted = m2.convert(b_val, *m1);\n   214→                let result = Decimal::from_f64(a_val + b_converted);\n   215→                Ok(Value::number_with_unit(result, Unit::Mass(*m1)))\n   216→            }\n   217→            (u1, u2) if u1 == u2 => Ok(Value::rational_with_unit(a + b, u1.clone())),\n   218→            (u1, u2) => Err(CalculatorError::unit_mismatch(\n   219→                \"add\",\n   220→                &u1.display_name(),\n   221→                &u2.display_name(),\n   222→            )),\n   223→        }\n   224→    }\n   225→\n   226→    fn add_numbers(\n   227→        &self,\n   228→        a: Decimal,\n   229→        b: Decimal,\n   230→        other: &Self,\n   231→        currency_db: &mut CurrencyDatabase,\n   232→        date: Option<&DateTime>,\n   233→    ) -> Result<Self, CalculatorError> {\n   234→        match (&self.unit, &other.unit) {\n   235→            (Unit::None, Unit::None) => Ok(Value::number(a + b)),\n   236→            (Unit::None, unit) | (unit, Unit::None) => {\n   237→                Ok(Value::number_with_unit(a + b, unit.clone()))\n   238→ u1.clone())),\n   251→            (u1, u2) => Err(CalculatorError::unit_mismatch(\n   252→                \"add\",\n   253→                &u1.display_name(),\n   254→                &u2.display_name(),\n   255→            )),\n   256→        }\n   257→    }\n   258→\n   259→    /// Subtracts two values.\n   260→    pub fn subtract(\n   261→        &self,\n   262→        other: &Self,\n   263→        currency_db: &mut CurrencyDatabase,\n   264→    ) -> Result<Self, CalculatorError> {\n   265→        self.subtract_at_date(other, currency_db, None)\n   266→    }\n   267→\n   268→    /// Subtracts two values with optional date context for historical currency conversion.\n   269→    pub fn subtract_at_date(\n   270→        &self,\n   271→        other: &Self,\n   272→        currency_db: &mut CurrencyDatabase,\n   273→        date: Option<&DateTime>,\n   274→    ) -> Result<Self, CalculatorError> {\n   275→        match (&self.kind, &other.kind) {\n   276→            // Rational - Rational\n   277→            (ValueKind::Rational(a), ValueKind::Rational(b)) => {\n   278→                self.subtract_rationals(a.clone(), b.clone(), other, currency_db, date)\n   279→            }\n   280→            // Number - Number (legacy)\n   281→            (ValueKind::Number(a), ValueKind::Number(b)) => {\n   282→                self.subtract_numbers(*a, *b, other, currency_db, date)\n   283→            }\n   284→            // Mixed: convert Decimal to Rational\n   285→            (ValueKind::Rational(a), ValueKind::Number(b)) => {\n   286→                let b_rat = Rational::from_decimal(*b);\n   287→                self.subtract_rationals(a.clone(), b_rat, other, currency_db, date)\n   288→            }\n   289→            (ValueKind::Number(a), ValueKind::Rational(b)) => {\n   290→                let a_rat = Rational::from_decimal(*a);\n   291→                self.subtract_rationals(a_rat, b.clone(), other, currency_db, date)\n   292→            }\n   293→            (ValueKind::DateTime(dt1), ValueKind::DateTime(dt2)) => {\n   294→                let diff = dt1.subtract(dt2);\n   295→                Ok(Value::duration(diff.as_secs() as i64))\n   296→            }\n   297→            (ValueKind::DateTime(dt), ValueKind::Duration { seconds }) => {\n   298→                Ok(Value::datetime(dt.add_duration(-seconds)))\n   299→            }\n   300→            (ValueKind::Duration { seconds: s1 }, ValueKind::Duration { seconds: s2 }) => {\n   301→                Ok(Value::duration(s1 - s2))\n   302→            }\n   303→            _ => Err(CalculatorError::InvalidOperation(format!(\n   304→                \"Cannot subtract {} from {}\",\n   305→                other.type_name(),\n   306→                self.type_name()\n   307→            ))),\n   308→        }\n   309→    }\n   310→\n   311→    fn subtract_rationals(\n   312→        &self,\n   313→        a: Rational,\n   314→        b: Rational,\n   315→        other: (Unit::Currency(c1), Unit::Currency(c2)) => {\n   329→                let a_dec = a.to_decimal();\n   330→                let b_dec = b.to_decimal();\n   331→                // Use historical rate if &u1.display_name(),\n   352→                &u2.display_name(),\n   353→            )),\n   354→        }\n   355→    }\n   356→\n   357→    fn subtract_numbers(\n   358→        &self,\n   359→                   (u1, u2) if u1 == u2 => Unit::None,\n   493→                    _ => self.unit.clone(),\n   494→                };\n   495→\n   496→       return Err(CalculatorError::DivisionByZero);\n   501→                }\n   502→                let a_rat = Rational::from_decimal(*a);\n   503→                let result = a_rat / b.clone();\n   504→\n   505→                let unit = match (&self.unit, &other.unit) {\n   506→                    (Unit::Currency(c1), Unit::Currency(c2)) if c1 == c2 => Unit::None,\n   507→                    (unit, Unit::None) => unit.clone(),\n   508→                    (Unit::None, _) => Unit::None,\n   509→                    (u1, u2) if u1 == u2 => Unit::None,\n   510→                    _ =>   ))),\n   534→        }\n   535→    }\n   536→\n   537→    /// Converts this value to the given unit.\n   538→    ///\n   539→    /// Supports conversion between data size units (KB, KiB, MB, MiB,    /// Negates the value.\n   610→    #[must_use]\n   611→    pub fn negate(&self) -> Self {\n   612→        match &self.kind {\n   613→            ValueKind::Number(n) => Value::number_with_unit(-*n, let body = format!(\n   362→        \"## Input that failed to parse\\n\\n```\\n{}\\n```\\n\\n## Error message\\n\\n```\\n{}\\n```\\n\\n## Expected behavior\\n\\nPlease describe what you expected the  let mut result = String::new();\n   381→    for c in s.chars() {\n   382→        match c {\n   383→            'A'..='Z' | 'a'..='z' | '0'..='9' | '-' | '_' | '.' | '~' => result.push(c),\n   384→              result.push_str(&format!(\"%{byte:02X}\"));\n   389→                }\n   390→            }\n   391→        }\n   392→    }\n   393→    result\n   394→}\n   395→\n   396→/// The main }\n   436→\n   437→    /// Updates exchange rates from API response. 442→            Ok(r) => r,\n   443→            Err(_) => return 0,\n   444→        };\n   445→\n   446→        let base_upper = base.to_uppercase();\n   447→        let timestamp = .set_rate_with_info(&base_upper, &target_upper, info);\n   463→\n   464→            count += 1;\n   465→        }\n   466→\n   467→        count\n   468→    }\n   469→\n   470→    /// Updates RUB \"eur\": 90.58, \"inr\": 0.842, ...}`\n   474→    /// where each value represents \"1 CURRENCY = X RUB\".\n   475→    ///\n   476→    /// These rates take priority over ECB/Frankfurter rates for RUB RUB amount).\n   480→    #[wasm_bindgen]\n   481→    pub fn update_cbr_rates_from_api(&mut self, date: &str, rates_json: &str) -> usize {\n   482→        let rates: std::collections::HashMap<String, f64> = match serde_json::from_str(rates_json) {\n   483→            Ok(r) => r,\n   484→            Err(_) => return 0,\n   485→        };\n   486→\n   487→        let timestamp = chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n   488→        let mut count = 0;\n   489→\n   490→        for (currency, rub_per_unit) in rates {\n   491→            let currency_upper = currency.to_uppercase();\n .with_fetched_at(&timestamp);\n   502→\n   503→            self.parser\n   504→                .currency_db_mut()\n   505→                .set_rate_with_info(&currency_upper, \"RUB\", info);\n   506→\n   507→            count += 1;\n   508→        }\n   509→\n   510→        count\n   511→    }\n   512→\n   513→    /// Updates cryptocurrency exchange rates from API response.\n   514→    /// count\n   548→    }\n   549→}\n   550→\n   551→impl Calculator {\n   552→    /// Internal calculation method that returns a proper Result type.\n   553→    pub fn calculate_internal(&mut self, input:        CalculationResult::symbolic(\n   565→                    &expression,\n   566→                    result,\n   567→                    latex_input,\n   568→                    latex_result,\n   569→                    plot_data,\n   570→                )\n   571→            }\n   572→            Err(e) => CalculationResult::failure_with_i18n(&e, input),\n   573→        }\n   574→    }\n   575→\n   576→    /// Generates plot data for an integral expression.\n   577→    fn generate_plot_data_for_integral(&mut self, input: &str) -> Option<PlotData> {\n   578→        // Try to parse and extract the integrand for plotting\n   579→        let expr = self.parser.parse(input).ok()?;\n   580→\n   581→        if let types::Expression::IndefiniteIntegral {\n   582→            integrand,\n   583→            variable,\n   584→        } = expr\n   585→        {\n   586→            // Generate plot points for the integrand\n   587→            let mut x_values = Vec::new();\n   588→            let mut y_values = Vec::new();\n   589→\n   590→            // Generate points from -10 to 10 with 200 steps\n   591→            let num_points: i32 = 200;\n   592→            let x_min = -10.0;\n   593→            let x_max = 10.0;\n   594→            let step = (x_max - x_min) / f64::from(num_points);\n   595→\n   596→            for i in 0..=num_points {\n   597→                let x = f64::from(i).mul_add(step, x_min);\n   598→\n   599→                // Skip x = 0 for functions like sin(x)/x to avoid division issues\n   600→                if x.abs() < 1e-10 {\n   601→                    // For sin(x)/x, the limit at x=0 is 1\n   602→                    x_values.push(x);\n   603→                    y_values.push(1.0);\n   604→                    continue;\n   605→                }\n   606→\n   607→                // Try to evaluate the integrand at this point\n   608→                if let Ok(y_val) = self.evaluate_at_point(&integrand, &variable, x) {\n   609→                    if y_val.is_finite() {\n   610→                        x_values.push(x);\n   611→                        y_values.push(y_val);\n   612→                    }\n   613→                }\n   614→            }\n   615→\n   616→            if !x_values.is_empty() {\n   617→                return Some(PlotData {\n   618→                    x_values,\n   619→                    y_values,\n   620→                    label: format!(\"{}\", integrand),\n   621→                    x_label: variable.clone(),\n   622→                    y_label: format!(\"f({})\", variable),\n   623→                });\n   624→            }\n   625→        }\n   626→\n   627→        None\n   628→    }\n   629→\n   630→    /// Evaluates an expression at a specific point.\n   631→    fn evaluate_at_point(\n   632→        &mut self,\n   633→        expr: &types::Expression,\n   634→        var: &str,\n   635→        value: f64,\n   636→    ) -> Result<f64, CalculatorError> {\n   637→        let substituted = expression.\n   646→    fn substitute_variable(expr: &types::Expression, var: &str, value: f64) -> types::Expression {\n   647→        use types::{Decimal, Expression};\n   648→\n   649→        match expr {\n   650→            Expression::Variable(name) if name == var => {\n   651→                Expression::number(Decimal::from_f64(value))\n   652→            }\n   653→            Expression::Variable(_) | Expression::Number { .. } | Expression::DateTime(_) => {\n   654→                expr.clone()\n   655→            }\n   656→            Expression::Binary { left, op, right }           ),\n   661→            Expression::Negate(inner) => {\n   662→                Expression::negate(Self::substitute_variable(inner, var, value))\n   663→            }\n   664→            Expression::Group(inner) => {\n   665→                Expression::group(Self::substitute_variable(inner, var, value))\n   666→            }\n   667→            Expression::Power { base, exponent } => Expression::power(\n   668→                Self::substitute_variable(base, var, value),\n   669→                Self::substitute_variable(exponent, var, value),\n   670→            ),\n   671→            Expression::FunctionCall { name, args } => Expression::function_call(\n   672→                name.clone(),\n   673→                args.iter()\n   674→                    .map(|a|           Self::substitute_variable(v, var, value),\n   679→                Self::substitute_variable(time, var, value),\n   680→            ),\n   681→            Expression::IndefiniteIntegral {\n   682→                integrand,\n   683→                variable,\n   684→            } => Expression::indefinite_integral(\n   685→                Self::substitute_variable(integrand, var, value),\n   686→                variable.clone(),\n   687→            ),\n   688→            Expression::UnitConversion {\n   689→                value: v,\n   690→                target_unit,\n   691→ }\n   697→\n   698→    /// Parses an expression without evaluating it.\n   699→    pub fn parse(&self, input: &str) -> Result<types::Expression, CalculatorError> {\n   700→        self.parser.parse(input)\n   701→    }\n   702→\n   703→    /// Evaluates a parsed expression.\n   704→    pub fn evaluate(&mut self, expr: &types::Expression) -> Result<Value, CalculatorError> {\n   705→        self.parser.evaluate(expr)\n   706→    }\n   707→\n   708→    /// Loads a historical exchange rate from .lino format content.\n   709→    ///\n   710→    /// The .lino format for rates:\n   711→    /// ```text\n   712→    /// rate:\n   713→    ///   from USD\n   714→    ///   to EUR\n   715→    ///   value 0.92\n   716→    ///   date 2026-01-25\n   717→    ///   source 'frankfurter.dev (ECB)'\n   718→    /// ```\n   719→    pub fn load_rate_from_lino(&mut self, content: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n   720→        let mut from_currency: Option<String> = None;\n   721→        let mut to_currency: Option<String> = None;\n   722→        let mut value: Option<f64> = None;\n   723→        let mut date: Option<String> = None;\n   724→        let mut source: Option<String> = None;\n   725→\n   726→        for line in content.lines() {\n   727→            let line = line.trim();\n   728→            if line.is_empty() || line == \"rate:\" {\n   729→                continue;\n   730→            }\n   731→\n   732→            if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"from \") {\n   733→                from_currency = Some(rest.trim().to_uppercase());\n   734→            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"to \") {\n   735→                to_currency = Some(rest.trim().to_uppercase());\n   736→            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"value \") {\n   737→                value = rest.trim().parse().ok();\n   738→            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"date \") {\n   739→                date = Some(rest.trim().to_string());\n   740→            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"source \") {\n   741→                // Remove quotes from source\n   742→                let src = rest.trim();\n   743→                let src = src.trim_start_matches('\\'').trim_end_matches('\\'');\n   744→                let src = src.trim_start_matches('\"').trim_end_matches('\"');\n   745→                source = Some(src.to_string());\n   746→            }\n   747→        }\n   748→\n   749→        let from = from_currency.ok_or(\"Missing 'from' currency\")?;\n   750→        let to = to_currency.ok_or(\"Missing 'to' currency\")?;\n   751→        let rate_value = value.ok_or(\"Missing 'value'\")?;\n   752→        let rate_date = date.ok_or(\"Missing 'date'\")?;\n   753→        let rate_source = source.unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".to_string());\n   754→\n   755→        // Create ExchangeRateInfo and add to the database\n   756→        let rate_info = types::ExchangeRateInfo::new(rate_value, rate_source, rate_date.clone());\n   757→\n   758→        self.parser\n   759→            .currency_db_mut()\n   760→            .set_historical_rate_with_info(&from, &to, &rate_date, rate_info);\n   761→\n   762→        Ok(())\n   763→    }\n   764→\n   765→    /// Loads multiple historical exchange rates from a batch of .lino content.\n   766→    /// Each rate should be separated by double newlines or start with \"rate:\".\n   767→    pub fn load_rates_batch(&mut self, contents: &[&str]) -> Result<usize, String> {\n   768→ 773→            // Silently skip invalid rate files\n   774→        }\n   775→        Ok(loaded)\n   776→    }\n   777→\n   778→    /// Loads historical exchange rates from a consolidated .lino Option<PlotData> {\n        // Try to parse and extract the integrand for plotting\n        let expr = self.parser.parse(input).ok()?;\n\n        if let types::Expression::IndefiniteIntegral {\n            integrand,\n            variable,\n        } = expr\n        {\n            // Generate plot points for the integrand\n            let mut x_values = Vec::new();\n            let mut y_values = Vec::new();\n\n            // Generate points from -10 to 10 with 200 steps\n            let num_points: i32 = 200;\n            let x_min = -10.0;\n            let x_max = 10.0;\n            let step = (x_max - x_min) / f64::from(num_points);\n\n            for i in 0..=num_points {\n                let x = f64::from(i).mul_add(step, x_min);\n\n                // Skip x = 0 for functions like sin(x)/x to avoid division issues\n                if x.abs() < 1e-10 {\n                    // For sin(x)/x, the limit at x=0 is 1\n                    x_values.push(x);\n                    y_values.push(1.0);\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                // Try to evaluate the integrand at this point\n                if let Ok(y_val) = self.evaluate_at_point(&integrand, &variable, x) {\n                    if y_val.is_finite() {\n                        x_values.push(x);\n                        y_values.push(y_val);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            if !x_values.is_empty() {\n                return Some(PlotData {\n                    x_values,\n                    y_values,\n     None\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluates an expression at a specific point.\n    fn evaluate_at_point(\n        &mut self,\n        expr: &types::Expression,\n        var: &str,\n        value: f64,\n    ) -> Result<f64, CalculatorError> {\n        let substituted = Self::substitute_variable(expr, var, value);\n        let result = self.parser.evaluate(&substituted)?;\n        result\n            .as_decimal()\n            .map(|d| d.to_f64())\n            .ok_or_else(|| CalculatorError::eval(\"Expected numeric result\"))\n    }\n\n    /// Substitutes a variable with a numeric value in an expression.\n    fn substitute_variable(expr: &types::Expression, var: &str, value: f64) -> types::Expression {\n        use types::{Decimal, Expression};\n\n        match expr {\n            Expression::Variable(name) if name == var => {\n                Expression::number(Decimal::from_f64(value))\n            }\n            Expression::Variable(_) | Expression::Number { .. } | Expression::DateTime(_) => {\n                expr.clone()\n            }\n            Expression::Binary { left, op, right } => Expression::binary(\n                Self::substitute_variable(left, var, value),\n                *op,\n                Self::substitute_variable(right, var, value),\n            ),\n            Expression::Negate(inner) => {\n                Expression::negate(Self::substitute_variable(inner, var, value))\n            }\n            Expression::Group(inner) => {\n                Expression::group(Self::substitute_variable(inner, var, value))\n            }\n            Expression::Power { base, exponent } => Expression::power(\n                Self::substitute_variable(base, var, value),\n                Self::substitute_variable(exponent, var, value),\n            ),\n            Expression::FunctionCall { name, args } => Expression::function_call(\n                name.clone(),\n                args.iter()\n                    .map(|a| Self::substitute_variable(a, var, value))\n                    .collect(),\n            ),\n            Expression::AtTime { value: v, time } => Expression::at_time(\n                Self::substitute_variable(v, var, value),\n                Self::substitute_variable(time, var, value),\n            ),\n            Expression::IndefiniteIntegral {\n                integrand,\n                variable,\n            } => Expression::indefinite_integral(\n                Self::substitute_variable(integrand, var, value),\n                variable.clone(),\n            ),\n            Expression::UnitConversion {\n                value: v,\n                target_unit,\n            } => Expression::unit_conversion(\n                Self::substitute_variable(v, var, value),\n                target_unit.clone(),\n            ),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Parses an expression without evaluating it.\n    pub fn parse(&self, input: &str) -> Result<types::Expression, CalculatorError> {\n        self.parser.parse(input)\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluates a parsed expression.\n    pub fn Common Timezone Abbreviations and UTC Offsets\n\n### North American Time Zones (Standard Time)\n- **AST** (Atlantic Standard Time) = UTC-4\n- **EST** (Eastern Standard Time) = UTC-5\n- **CST** (Central Standard Time) = UTC-6\n- **MST** (Mountain Standard Time) = UTC-7\n- **PST** (Pacific Standard Time) = UTC-8\n- **AKST** (Alaska Standard Time) = UTC-9\n- **HST** (Hawaii Standard Time) = UTC-10\n\n### Daylight Saving Time Variants\nWhen DST is in effect, add one hour to standard time:\n- **EDT** (Eastern Daylight Time) = UTC-4\n- **CDT** (Central Daylight Time) = UTC-5\n- **MDT** (Mountain Daylight Time) = UTC-6\n- **PDT** (Pacific Daylight Time) = UTC-7\n\n### Critical Ambiguity Issues\n\n**Major Finding**: Timezone abbreviations are **highly ambiguous** and their use is discouraged:\n- **CST** can mean: China Standard Time (UTC+8), Cuba Standard Time (UTC-5), or Central Standard Time (UTC-6)\n- **CDT** can mean: Central Daylight Time or Cuba Daylight Time\n- **IST** can refer to: India, Ireland, or Israel time\n\n**Best Practice**: According to IANA tz database documentation and ISO 8601 standards, timezone abbreviations should be avoided in production code. Instead, use:\n1. **IANA region/city format**: `America/Chicago`, `America/New_York`, `America/Los_Angeles`\n2. **Numeric UTC offsets**: `-0600`, `-0500`, `-0800`\n\n## 2. Rust Libraries for Natural Language Date Parsing\n\n### Available Crates\n\n**1. natural-date-parser**\n- Designed to parse human-friendly expressions like \"next Monday,\" \"tomorrow at 5 PM,\" \"3 weeks from now\"\n- Built using the Pest parsing library\n- Recognizes various natural language phrases for dates and times\n\n**2. date_time_parser**\n- Built on chrono and regex crates\n- Provides extensive coverage of natural language statements\n- Allows parsing relative to current date/time OR custom date/time\n- Can handle phrases like \"Monday January 26th\"\n\n**3. fuzzydate**\n- Parses human-friendly phrases: \"five days after this Friday,\" \"tomorrow at noon,\" \"3 weeks ago\"\n- Returns chrono DateTime objects\n- Good for natural language scheduling\n\n**4. event_parser**\n- Leverages date_time_parser for parsing dates and times of events\n- Accepts English natural language event descriptions\n- Uses `to_event` function for parsing\n\n**5. timewarp**\n- NLP library for English and German natural language\n- Leverages pest for parsing human-readable dates and times\n- Supports multiple languages\n\n### Parsing Formats in Chrono\n\nFor structured date parsing (not natural language), chrono provides:\n- `DateTime::parse_from_rfc2822()` - e.g., \"Tue, 1 Jul 2003 10:52:37 +0200\"\n- `DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339()` - e.g., \"1996-12-19T16:39:57-08:00\"\n- `DateTime::parse_from_str()` - custom formats with format strings\n\n## 3. Handling Timezone Abbreviations in Rust\n\n### Chrono Limitations\n\n**Key Finding**: The chrono crate does **NOT** support parsing timezone abbreviations from input strings due to ambiguity:\n- The `%Z` format specifier only **prints** the offset when formatting\n- The timezone abbreviation will NOT be printed\n- It's not possible to reliably convert from abbreviation to offset\n\n### Recommended Approach: chrono-tz\n\nFor proper timezone support in Rust:\n- Use the **chrono-tz** crate (implements TimeZone trait for chrono)\n- Generated from IANA database using zoneinfo_parse\n- Supports full IANA timezone names via `FromStr` trait\n- Examples: `\"Antarctica/South_Pole\"`, `\"America/New_York\"`\n- Pretty-printing uses correct abbreviations (e.g., \"2016-05-10 12:00:00 BST\")\n\n### Working with Offsets\n\nFor explicit UTC offsets (not abbreviations):\n- Use `DateTime::parse_from_str` with `%z` format specifier\n- Handles offset notation like \"+0000\" or \"+00:00\"\n- More reliable than abbreviations\n\n## 4. Implementing \"now\" in Datetime Tools\n\n### Common Implementations\n\n**JavaScript (2026)**\n- Temporal API (shipped in Chrome 144, January 2026; Firefox 139, May 2025)\n- `Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO()` returns current date/time as ZonedDateTime\n- Modern replacement for Date object\n\n**Rust with Chrono**\n- `Utc::now()` - Current time in UTC\n- `Local::now()` - Current time in local timezone\n- Returns `DateTime<Utc>` or `DateTime<Local>` objects\n\nExample:\n```rust\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Local, Utc};\nlet current_utc: DateTime<Utc> = Utc::now();\nlet current_local: DateTime<Local> = Local::now();\n```\n\n**Python**\n- `dateparser.parse()` handles relative expressions like \"1 hour ago\"\n- `dateutil.parser` supports various formats with parserinfo parameters\n- Custom functions can parse \"5 minutes ago\" or \"2 days ago\"\n\n**C++ (2026)**\n- `std::chrono` remains standard for robust, timezone-aware datetime handling\n\n### Implementation Pattern\n\nThe \"now\" keyword is **NOT** typically parsed from strings. Rust Libraries for Natural Language Date Parsing\n\n### Available Crates\n\n**1. natural-date-parser**\n- Designed to parse human-friendly expressions like \"next Monday,\" \"tomorrow at 5 PM,\" \"3 weeks from now\"\n- Built using the Pest parsing library\n- Recognizes various natural language phrases for dates and times\n\n**2. date_time_parser**\n- Built on chrono and regex crates\n- Provides extensive coverage of natural language statements\n- Allows parsing relative to current date/time OR custom date/time\n- Can handle phrases like \"Monday January 26th\"\n\n**3. fuzzydate**\n- Parses human-friendly phrases: \"five days after this Friday,\" \"tomorrow at noon,\" \"3 weeks ago\"\n- Returns chrono DateTime objects\n- Good for natural language scheduling\n\n**4. event_parser**\n- Leverages date_time_parser for parsing dates and times of events\n- Accepts English natural language event descriptions\n- Uses `to_event` function for parsing\n\n**5. timewarp**\n- NLP library for English and German natural language\n- Leverages pest for parsing human-readable dates and times\n- Supports multiple languages\n\n### Parsing Formats in Chrono\n\nFor structured date parsing (not natural language), chrono provides:\n- `DateTime::parse_from_rfc2822()` - e.g., \"Tue, 1 Jul 2003 10:52:37 +0200\"\n- `DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339()` - e.g., \"1996-12-19T16:39:57-08:00\"\n- `DateTime::parse_from_str()` - custom formats with format strings\n\n## 3. Handling Timezone Abbreviations in Rust\n\n### Chrono Limitations\n\n**Key Finding**: The chrono crate does **NOT** support parsing timezone abbreviations from input strings due to ambiguity:\n- The `%Z` format specifier only **prints** the offset when formatting\n- The timezone abbreviation will NOT be printed\n- It's not possible to reliably convert from abbreviation to offset\n\n### Recommended Approach: chrono-tz\n\nFor proper timezone support in Rust:\n- Use the **chrono-tz** crate (implements TimeZone trait for chrono)\n- Generated from IANA database using zoneinfo_parse\n- Supports full IANA timezone names via `FromStr` trait\n- Examples: `\"Antarctica/South_Pole\"`, `\"America/New_York\"`\n- Pretty-printing uses correct abbreviations (e.g., \"2016-05-10 12:00:00 BST\")\n\n### Working with Offsets\n\nFor explicit UTC offsets (not abbreviations):\n- Use `DateTime::parse_from_str` with `%z` format specifier\n- Handles offset notation like \"+0000\" or \"+00:00\"\n- More reliable than abbreviations\n\n## 4. Implementing \"now\" in Datetime Tools\n\n### Common Implementations\n\n**JavaScript (2026)**\n- Temporal API (shipped in Chrome 144, January 2026; Firefox 139, May 2025)\n- `Temporal.Now.zonedDateTimeISO()` returns current date/time as ZonedDateTime\n- Modern replacement for Date object\n\n**Rust with Chrono**\n- `Utc::now()` - Current time in UTC\n- `Local::now()` - Current time in local timezone\n- Returns `DateTime<Utc>` or `DateTime<Local>` objects\n\nExample:\n```rust\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Local, Utc};\nlet current_utc: DateTime<Utc> = Utc::now();\nlet current_local: DateTime<Local> = Local::now();\n```\n\n**Python**\n- `dateparser.parse()` handles relative expressions like \"1 hour ago\"\n- `dateutil.parser` supports various formats with parserinfo parameters\n- Custom functions can parse \"5 minutes ago\" or \"2 days ago\"\n\n**C++ (2026)**\n- `std::chrono` remains standard for robust, timezone-aware datetime handling\n\n### Implementation Pattern\n\nThe \"now\" keyword is **NOT** typically parsed from strings. Instead:\n1. Detect the keyword \"now\" in input\n2. Replace it with actual current time using `Utc::now()` or equivalent\n3. Proceed with normal datetime operations\n\n## 5. \"Until\" as Time Difference Operator\n\n### Findings on \"Until\" Operator\n\n**Go Programming Language**\n- `time.Until(deadline)` is a standard idiom\n- Robust against wall clock resets\n- Returns duration by subtracting times\n- Similar to `Since`, `Before`, `After`, `Add`, `Equal`, `Compare`\n\n**General Pattern**\n- Most datetime calculators use **only `+` and `-` operators**\n- Valid expressions: \"1d 2h 3m 4s + 4h 5s - 2030s\"\n- \"Until\" is not a standard operator in most calculators\n\n### Time Difference Calculation Best Practices\n\n**Common Methods Across Languages:**\n\n1. **Go**: `time.Sub(t)` returns duration `t-u`\n2. **Python**: Subtract datetime objects to get timedelta, then convert to desired units\n3. **Java**: `Duration.between(t1, t2).toNanos()`\n4. **PHP**: `DateTimeInterface::diff()` returns DateInterval object\n\n**Implementation Approach for \"Until\":**\n- Treat \"until\" as a **duration calculation** between two timestamps\n- Calculate: `end_time - start_time`\n- Return the difference in appropriate units (days, hours, minutes, seconds)\n\n### Date Calculators Pattern\n\nDate calculators typically:\n1. Accept a starting point\n2. Choose direction (forward/backward)\n3. Enter time amount to adjust\n4. Calculate result or duration between points\n\n---\n\n## Sources\n\n- [JavaScript Temporal in 2026 - Bryntum](https://bryntum.com/blog/javascript-temporal-is-it-finally-here/)\n- [dateparser – Python parser documentation](https://dateparser.readthedocs.io/)\n- [dateutil parser documentation](https://dateutil.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parser.html)\n- [chrono-tz -     "content": "# Case Study: Issue #45 - Issue with expression: `Jan 27, 9:33am UTC`\n\n## Timeline of Events\n\n1. **User Input**: `Jan 27, 9:33am UTC`\n2. **Result**: `2026-01-27 09:33:00 +00:00` (successfully parsed)\n3. **Issue**: When input is a standalone date, the result should show a countdown (future) or elapsed time (past), not just echo back the datetime\n\n## Root Cause Analysis\n\nThe parser correctly parses `Jan 27, 9:33am UTC` as a DateTime value. However, the evaluator simply returns the DateTime as-is without computing any relationship to the current time.\n\nCurrently, `Expression::DateTime(dt)` evaluates to `Value::datetime(dt.clone())`, and `Value::datetime` displays as the formatted datetime string. There is no logic to compute the difference from \"now\".\n\n### Secondary Issue: Links Notation\nThe issue also states that composite datetime expressions should be enclosed in parentheses in links notation, like `(2026-01-27 09:33:00 +00:00)`. Currently, `Expression::DateTime` in `to_lino()` just returns `dt.to_string()` without wrapping.\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\nPer the issue:\n1. **Date-only input**: When a user enters just a date/time, show the time difference from now\n   - If in the future: show countdown (\"in X days, Y hours, Z minutes\")\n   - If in the past: show elapsed time (\"X days, Y hours, Z minutes ago\")\n2. **Links notation**: Always enclose dates as links like `(2026-01-27 09:33:00 +00:00)` in links notation\n\n## Proposed Solution\n\n### 1. Show time difference for standalone datetime input\nWhen the expression is a single DateTime (not part of an arithmetic operation):\n- Calculate the difference between the input datetime and current UTC time\n- Show both the parsed datetime AND the duration from now in the steps\n- The result remains the datetime, but steps include \"Time from now: X days, Y hours ago\" or \"Time until: X days, Y hours\"\n\n### 2. Update links notation for DateTime\nIn `Expression::to_lino()`, wrap DateTime values in parentheses: `(datetime_string)`.\n\n## Implementation Approach\n\nSince the frontend handles dynamic ticking (as mentioned in the issue: \"interactive ticking onwards\"), the backend should:\n1. Return the parsed DateTime value as the result\n2. Include the current difference in the steps for initial display\n3. The frontend can use the DateTime value to compute live updates\n\n## Related Concepts\n\n- Time duration formatting: days, hours, minutes, seconds\n- Relative time display (e.g., \"2 days ago\", \"in 3 hours\")\n- Live/ticking countdowns require frontend JavaScript implementation\n\n## Data Files\n\n- Input expression: `Jan 27, 9:33am UTC`\n- Parsed result: `2026-01-27 09:33:00 +00:00`\n- Environment: Version 0.1.0, Safari on macOS\n",

   /// Links notation uses minimal parentheses, only adding them where\n    /// necessary to clarify structure. The rules are:\n    /// - Atomic values (numbers, variables) don't need parentheses\n    /// - Binary operations are wrapped in a single set of parentheses\n    /// - Explicit groups from the input Self::Number { value, unit } => {\n                let num_str = value.to_string();\n                if *unit == Unit::None {\n                    num_str\n                } else {\n format!(\"({expr_str})\")\n            }\n            Self::Negate(inner) => {\n                let inner_str = inner.to_lino_internal(None);\n                // Only add parens if the inner expression needs them\n                if inner.needs_parens_for_unary() {\n                    format!(\"(-({inner_str}))\")\n                } else {\n                    format!(\"(-{inner_str})\")\n                }\n            }\n            Self::Group(inner) => {\n                // Groups are explicitly requested by the user\n                // If the inner expression already has its own parentheses, don't double-wrap\n                let inner_str = inner.to_lino_internal(None);\n                if inner_str.starts_with('(') && inner_str.ends_with(')')     let value_str = value.to_lino_internal(None);\n                let time_str = time.to_lino_internal(None);\n                format!(\"({value_str} at {time_str})\")\n            }\n            Self::FunctionCall { name, args } => {\n                if args.is_empty() {\n                    name.clone()\n                } else {\n                    let args_str = args\n                        .iter()\n                        .map(|a| a.to_lino_internal(None))\n                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                        .join(\", \");\n                    format!(\"{name}({args_str})\")\n                }\n            }\n            Self::Variable(name) => name.clone(),\n            Self::Power { base, exponent } => {\n                let base_str = base.needs_parens_for_power() {\n                    format!(\"({base_str})^{exp_str}\")\n                } else {\n                    format!(\"{base_str}^{exp_str}\")\n                }\n             format!(\"({value_str} as {target_unit})\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this expression needs parentheses when used as a unary operand.\n    fn needs_parens_for_unary(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(\n            self,\n            Self::Binary { .. } | Self::AtTime { .. } | Self::UnitConversion { .. }\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Returns   }\n\n    /// Parse an integrand expression up to (but not including) the position `until_pos`.\n    fn parse_integrand_until(&mut self, until_pos: usize) -> Result<Expression, CalculatorError> {\n DateTimeGrammar::new(),\n            currency_db: CurrencyDatabase::new(),\n            current_date_context: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a reference to the currency database.\n    pub &mut self,\n        input: &str,\n    ) -> Result<(Value, Vec<String>, String), CalculatorError> {\n        let input = input.trim();\n        if input.is_empty() {\n            return parser.parse_expression()\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluates an expression.\n    pub fn evaluate(&mut self, expr: &Expression) -> Result<Value, CalculatorError> {\n        self.evaluate_expr(expr)\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluates an expression with step-by-step tracking.\n    fn evaluate_with_steps(\n        &mut self,\n        expr: &Expression,\n    ) -> Result<(Value, Vec<String>), CalculatorError> {\n        let mut steps = Vec::new();\n\n        steps.push(format!(\"Input expression: {expr}\"));\n\n        let result = self.evaluate_expr_with_steps(expr, &mut steps)?;\n\n        steps.push(format!(\"Final result: {}\", result.to_display_string()));\n\n        Ok((result, steps))\n    }\n\n    fn evaluate_expr(&mut self, expr: &Expression) -> Result<Value, CalculatorError> {\n        match expr {\n            Expression::Number { value, unit } => {\n                // Convert to Rational for exact arithmetic\n                let rational = Rational::from_decimal(*value);\n                Ok(Value::rational_with_unit(rational, unit.clone()))\n            }\n            Expression::DateTime(dt) => Ok(Value::datetime(dt.clone())),\n            Expression::Now => Ok(Value::duration(seconds))\n                    }\n                    _ => Err(CalculatorError::InvalidOperation(\n                        \"until requires a datetime expression\".into(),\n                    )),\n                }\n            }\n            Expression::Binary { left, op, right } => {\n                let left_val = self.evaluate_expr(left)?;\n                let right_val = self.evaluate_expr(right)?;\n                self.apply_binary_op(&left_val, *op, &right_val)\n            }\n            Expression::Negate(inner) => {\n                let val = Evaluate all arguments\n                let mut arg_values = Vec::new();\n                for arg in args {\n                    let val = self.evaluate_expr(arg)?;\n                    // Extract the })?;\n                    arg_values.push(decimal);\n                }\n\n                // Call the function\n                let result = evaluate_function(name, &arg_values)?;\n                Ok(Value::number(result))\n            }\n            Expression::Variable(name) => {\n                // Variables should not appear in direct evaluation\n                // They are only used in CalculatorError::InvalidOperation(\"power base must be numeric\".into())\n                })?;\n                let exp_dec = exp_val.as_decimal().ok_or_else(|| {\n                    CalculatorError::InvalidOperation(\"power exponent must be numeric\".into())\n                })?;\n\n                let base_f64 = base_dec.to_f64();\n                let exp_f64 =      self.current_date_context = old_context;\n\n                result\n            }\n            Expression::FunctionCall { name, args } => {\n                let name_lower = name.to_lowercase();\n\n                // Special handling for integrate(expr, var, lower, upper)\n                if name_lower == \"integrate\" {\n                    steps.push(format!(\"Numerical }\n            Expression::Variable(name) => {\n                Err(CalculatorError::eval(format!(\"undefined variable: {name}\")))\n            }\n            Expression::Power { base, exponent } => {\n                let base_val = self.evaluate_expr_with_steps(base, steps)?;\n                let exp_val = self.evaluate_expr_with_steps(exponent, steps)?;\n\n                steps.push(format!(\n }\n\n                let val = Value::number(Decimal::from_f64(result));\n                steps.push(format!(\"= {}\", val.to_display_string()));\n                Ok(val)\n            }\n            Expression::IndefiniteIntegral {\n                integrand,\n                variable,\n            } => {\n                steps.push(format!(\n                    \"Indefinite integral: ∫ {} an integrate function call: integrate(expr, var, lower, upper).\n    ///\n    /// Uses numerical integration (Simpson's rule) to compute the definite integral.\n    #[allow(clippy::many_single_char_names)]\n    fn evaluate_integrate(&mut self, args: &[Expression]) -> Result<Value, CalculatorError> {\n        if args.len() != 4 {\n            return Err(CalculatorError::invalid_args(\n                \"integrate\",\n                \"expected 4 arguments: integrate(expr, var, lower, upper)\",\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // Second argument must be a variable name\n        let var_name = match &args[1] {\n            Expression::Variable(name) => name.clone(),\n            _ => {\n                return Err(CalculatorError::invalid_args(\n                    \"integrate\",\n                    \"second argument must be a variable name (e.g., x)\",\n                ))\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Evaluate lower and upper bounds\n        let lower_val = self.evaluate_expr(&args[2])?;\n        let lower = lower_val.as_decimal().ok_or_else(|| {\n            CalculatorError::invalid_args(\"integrate\", \"lower bound must be numeric\")\n        })?;\n\n        let upper_val = self.evaluate_expr(&args[3])?;\n        let upper = upper_val.as_decimal().ok_or_else(|| {\n            CalculatorError::invalid_args(\"integrate\", \"upper bound must be numeric\")\n        })?;\n\n        let a = lower.to_f64();\n        let b = upper.to_f64();\n\n        // The expression to integrate\n        let integrand = &args[0];\n\n        // Numerical integration using Simpson's rule\n        let n = 1000_usize; // Number of subdivisions\n        let h = (b - a) / (n as f64);\n\n        let mut sum = 0.0;\n\n        // f(a) + f(b)\n        sum += self.evaluate_at(integrand, &var_name, a)?.to_f64();\n        sum += self.evaluate_at(integrand, &var_name, b)?.to_f64();\n\n        // 4 * sum of odd terms\n        for i in (1..n).step_by(2) {\n            let x = (i as f64).mul_add(h, a);\n            sum += 4.0 * self.evaluate_at(integrand, &var_name, x)?.to_f64();\n        }\n\n        // 2 * sum of even terms\n        for i in (2..n).step_by(2) {\n            let x = (i as f64).mul_add(h, a);\n            sum += 2.0 * self.evaluate_at(integrand, &var_name, x)?.to_f64();\n        }\n\n        let result = sum * h / 3.0;\n\n        if result.is_nan() {\n            return Err(CalculatorError::domain(\"integration result is undefined\"));\n        }\n        if result.is_infinite() {\n            return Err(CalculatorError::Overflow);\n        }\n\n        Ok(Value::number(Decimal::from_f64(result)))\n    }\n\n    /// Evaluates an expression with a variable substitution.\n    fn evaluate_at(\n        &mut self,\n        expr: &Expression,\n        var_name: &str,\n        value: f64,\n    ) -> Result<Decimal, CalculatorError> {\n        let val = self.evaluate_expr_with_var(expr, var_name, Decimal::from_f64(value))?;\n unit.clone()))\n            }\n            Expression::DateTime(dt) => Ok(Value::datetime(dt.clone())),\n            Expression::Binary { left, op, right } => {\n                let left_val =        }\n            Expression::Group(inner) => self.evaluate_expr_with_var(inner, var_name, var_value),\n            Expression::AtTime { value, time } => {\n                let _time_val = this is a breaking change\n\n### Removed\n- Removed deprecated `legacy_mode` option\n```\n\n## Why Fragments?\n\nUsing changelog fragments (similar to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) in JavaScript and [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/) in Python):\n\n1. **No merge conflicts**: Multiple PRs can add fragments without conflicts\n2. **Per-PR documentation**: Each PR documents its own changes\n3. **Automated version bumping**: Version bump type is specified per-change\n4. **Automated collection**: Fragments are automatically collected during release\n5. **Consistent format**: Template ensures consistent changelog entries\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **During PR**: Add a fragment file with your changes and bump type\n2. **On merge to main**: The release workflow automatically:\n   - Reads all fragment files and determines the highest bump type\n   - Bumps the version in `Cargo.toml` accordingly\n   - Collects fragments into `CHANGELOG.md`\n   - Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n   - Removes processed fragment files\n\n## Multiple PRs and Bump Priority\n\nWhen multiple PRs are merged before a release, all pending fragments are processed together. The **highest** bump type wins:\n\n- If any fragment specifies `major`, the release is a major version bump\n- Otherwise, if any specifies `minor`, the release is a minor version bump\n- Otherwise, the release is a patch version bump\n\nThis ensures that breaking changes are never missed, even when combined with smaller changes.\n\n## Default Behavior\n\nIf a fragment doesn't include a bump type in the frontmatter, it defaults to `patch`.\n",
